answer: Every agent carries an atlas of signed voyage receipts: a lantern-lit ledger of real deliveries, each receipt countersigned by the counterparty and bonded by a refundable stake. A new identity starts dark and earns trust only by completing paid work, one receipt at a time, while its stake is slashed if fraud is proven. Forging a hundred fake identities therefore costs a hundred voyages of real work plus a hundred stakes at risk, while one honest agent climbs once and keeps its reputation.
